Didn't this guy have better things to do at the club other than stand here and judge everyone's drink orders?

“Does anyone know anyone else at this club?” The random man was situated at the very end of the bar, leaning against the counter with a glass set upon its surface. Phainon squinted at the cup to see what this guy had happened to order, since his taste in drinks was just so much more elite, apparently, but it was dark in the club with only blue lights blinking in and out to the beat of the music. All Phainon could see was that the drink was a dark red. He could barely even see the guy he was talking to either; all he could tell was that he was wearing all black, and his hair reached his shoulders.

The drive back home had made him sleepy, especially from how exhausted he was from everything he had gone through. Eyes widening, he immediately sat up in bed. That reminded him; he never texted that man when he returned home. He had immediately collapsed in bed upon arriving at his apartment, and all of his friends went to find their own places to sleep somewhere around his apartment. Phainon glanced around his bedroom and realized that no one was in there, which meant they were all crowded in his living room.

He was still wearing the same clothes he was wearing at the club, which was kind of gross, but he was also way too tired to change out of them when he arrived home last night. Resolving himself to do his sheets later when his friends left, Phainon dug his hands into his pockets to find the number that Mydei left for him. Only to realize that his pockets were still empty–as empty as they were when he was trying to find his phone for Mydei.

There was no way; Phainon refused to believe it. He jumped up in bed, shoving his hands as deeply as he could into every single pocket that existed on his jeans, but to no avail. Every single pocket was empty, and there wasn't a single cocktail napkin in his grasp.

Perhaps, did he dream up the entirety of last night?!

And second of all, how did Phainon miraculously meet the man of his dreams just by existing in the club that day? It was then that Phainon realized Castorice definitely witnessed him shoving his tongue down some stranger's throat and grinding his body against that stranger too, and he couldn't help but blush himself at recalling the dream. Was he really getting it on right at the bar in front of the club entrance? The bar was right where you walked into the club.

“Um… Yes…” Poor Castorice's voice was barely above a whisper, and there was no doubt in Phainon's mind that her face was burning hot even without touching her. “He was… um…” She furrowed her eyebrows in an attempt to recall the face of a stranger that she had seen in a dimly lit, crowded club. “Blonde hair that went to his shoulders? He was very well-built too.”

“So he was there?!” Phainon stepped over Anaxa's sleeping body to quickly approach the woman. “He was real?!”

“Real?” Castorice's eyes widened. “Didn't he write his number for you?”

“He gave you his number?!” Hyacine was practically squealing now. “Wait, Castorice, what was Phainon doing when you found him?! Tell me!”

“I don't have his number anymore!” Phainon cried. “I searched everywhere in my pockets, but it's not there!”

“Castorice, what was he doing?!”

“Castorice, do you remember his number?!”

Two people were wailing in the living room for two very different things, and Aglaea had to shut both of them up before Castorice became overwhelmed, which was already too late because it already seemed as if Castorice's brain had become fried. This was probably the last time Castorice would ever wake up so early in the morning.

“Enough!”

All four people on the sofa bed froze at the sound of a new voice entering the conversation, and Phainon rigidly turned around to find Anaxa's sharp glare boring straight into him. He was now standing up from the floor, appearing both sleep-deprived and annoyed.

With a light, nervous chuckle, Phainon did his best to smile at him. “Good morning… Anaxa.”

“Do not call me that this early in the morning.” Anaxa harshly snapped. “The hell are you guys moaning and groaning about at nine in the damn morning? Were we not out until three last night?”

“Sorry, Anaxa.” Three voices rang in unison. Aglaea only chuckled in amusement.

“Shut up and answer my question.”

Phainon frowned. “How do I shut up and answer your question at the same time?”

“Do not get smart with me, Phainon.” Anaxa clicked his tongue. “Answer me, or you owe me for waking me up so early.”

Phainon was sure he already owed Anaxa for waking him up at nine in the morning, but he answered nonetheless. “I was asking Castorice if she remembered the man I was with at the club last night.”

“And?”

“And he gave me his number on a napkin, but I can't find it in my pockets anymore.”

Anaxa grunted and turned to Hyacine. “So, what are you grumbling about at nine in the morning?”

“I just wanted to know what Phainon was doing with this man.” Hyacine wilted under Anaxa's sharp glare.

With crossed arms, Anaxa turned to Phainon. “So, what were you doing with this stranger?”

“I was… uh…” Phainon's face, which had previously cooled down from earlier, began to heat up once more at the memory. “I was… making out with this guy at the bar.”

Aglaea's eyes widened, and Hyacine sharply gasped.

“Phainon!” Hyacine blushed herself. “You were making out with some random guy at the club?!”

“It wasn't on purpose!” Phainon cried, earning four very dubious stares. “Well… It was… Okay, yes, I did mean to make out with him, but it wasn't the plan for last night to make out with anyone!”

“Does anyone ever plan that?” Anaxa rolled his eye. Anaxa had, unfortunately, been in an accident that took both his older sister's life and one of his eyes. Because of that, he always wore an eyepatch on one side of his face. “So, you made out with this guy, he gave you his number, and you lost it.”

“I didn't lose it! I–” Phainon began desperately searching his pockets once more, but once again, to no avail.

“You lost it,” Anaxa repeated.

Phainon's shoulders slumped in defeat. “Yes… I lost it. I put it in my pocket, but it's not there anymore.”

“Which pocket?” Anaxa eyed Phainon's jeans as if trying to assess which pocket the cocktail napkin was in.

“I swear it was this one.” Phainon patted his right front pocket. “But, there's nothing there. There's nothing in any of my pockets.”

Anaxa fell deep into thought while Hyacine shoved her own hands into Phainon's pockets as if she couldn't believe the number had been lost as well. Phainon frowned but let Hyacine continue her ministrations, and she looked plenty defeated once she had searched all his front and back pockets.

“I want to meet this guy you were making out with.” Hyacine pouted. “What was his name? Or, were you too busy sucking each other's mouths to exchange names?”

“Mydei!” Phainon grew bright red. He couldn't believe Hyacine was talking like that. “His name was Mydei, and no, we were not too busy sucking each other's mouths!”

Castorice cleared her throat, drawing the attention of everyone sitting on the couch. “Phainon… I actually called you six times before you heard me.”

“Six?!” Phainon and Hyacine both cried.

“How long were you standing there?!” The blush on Phainon's face only continued to grow.

“I didn't mean to keep watching, but you didn't hear me!” Castorice quickly retorted, her own face turning bright red once more. “You were… just so into him.”

“Castorice!” Phainon covered his face, trying to hide from the sheer embarrassment of his own friend watching him get it on with some stranger in the club. Both Aglaea and Hyacine laughed, with Aglaea pitifully patting Phainon's shoulder, and it was then that it was Anaxa's turn to clear his throat.

“Wait, Cas!” Hyacine suddenly exclaimed and began shaking her friend’s shoulders, interrupting whatever Anaxa had been preparing to say. “You need to tell me everything. All the details! Everything that they were doing! Where were they?! What was their position?! What was the guy wearing?!”

Phainon shot his head back up. “Castorice, don't tell her!” He wailed.

Hyacine and Phainon began pestering Castorice, bickering with each other in an attempt to talk over the other person. Poor Castorice was overwhelmed as she tried to calm the two people in front of her while being violently shaken by Hyacine's hands, with only Aglaea watching and laughing at the scene before her. It wasn't until Anaxa's voice rang clearly above everyone else's was Castorice finally saved.

“Your right front pocket was kicked when you were trying to carry Cipher,” Anaxa plainly stated as if he was able to replay the entirety of last night in his mind. “Actually, your entire being was kicked and punched by Cipher last night. I wouldn't be surprised if she knocked it out of your pocket.”

Phainon's eyes widened as he turned toward the completely oblivious woman who was still knocked out on his table. “It was Cipher?!”

“That's the only logical reasoning.” Anaxa nonchalantly shrugged. “Unless some pickpocket took the napkin, which I doubt.”

It was official: Cipher definitely owed Phainon when she woke up. In fact, she would owe him for the rest of her life. One, for cockblocking him, and two, for making him lose the only contact he had with the man of his literal dreams.

“You remember his name, right?” Anaxa spoke once more. “If he has social media, you might be able to find him with some work.”

Phainon's gaze snapped back to Anaxa. “You're right! Holy–Aglaea, could you hand me my phone?”

Aglaea quickly reached for her purse, rummaging through and unearthing Phainon's phone. Surprisingly, it still had battery, and Phainon quickly pulled up the first social media app he could find on his phone. He had stared at the napkin for so long that he remembered exactly how his name was spelled; unfortunately, he could not remember the ten digits that were also written right next to his name.

With four heads leering over his shoulder, Phainon could only find an account with the username “Mydeimos”. The following social media accounts were all some version of Mydeimos fan accounts, most likely for the first user showing up in the search results. The profile pictures were too small for anyone to accurately see who the person was in the photos.

“Mydeimos?” Phainon frowned. “That's not his name, though. How would I be able to search for just ‘Mydei’?”

“What if it is?” Anaxa remarked. “Just click on it.”

“But, why would he have fan accounts then?”

“Just fucking click on it.”

Phainon immediately clicked on it, and when the account loaded on his screen, a gasp resounded from Castorice right next to his head, and Phainon felt the air in his lungs completely still.

It was him.

This Mydeimos guy, who had loaded up on his phone screen, whose account basically consisted of concert recordings, interviews, magazine covers, professional photoshoots, and music video clips, was the guy that Phainon was arguing with, pushing against the wall, and making out with in the club last night. It finally clicked now, why Mydei had asked him if Phainon knew him last night. He was definitely used to people staring at him from being recognized as a rockstar, and he probably thought Phainon had recognized him too, after all the obvious staring Phainon was doing.

Three heads turned toward Castorice, who had gasped at the account, and she quickly shut her mouth that was agape.

“It's… That's him,” Castorice barely managed, swallowing dryly the more Phainon scrolled through the account. Even he was also in complete shock.

“Him?!” Hyacine practically screamed and whipped her head toward Phainon. “Phainon, you were making out with a celebrity?!”

“I–That's–” Phainon's mouth flapped open and closed, with no sound coming out of his throat. He kept scrolling through all the posts, but all he could see was just how talented this, apparently, rockstar was. There was no way this was the guy he was with last night, right? Surely, it must be a doppelganger? The more he scrolled through the account, the more his disbelief continued to grow, but there was no denying that this Mydeimos was exactly the guy he met at the club.

“A celebrity?!”

Five heads turned toward this new individual who had somehow squeezed herself onto the couch at some point while they were looking over the social media account, and there Cipher was, looking as cheeky and smug as ever. “Phainon, you know someone famous?!”

“It's all your fault!” Phainon had to restrain himself from jumping the woman right then and there.

“What? What do you mean?”

“I lost his number because of you!”

“Phainon! How dare you lose a famous person’s number!”

“It was literally your fault!” Phainon groaned and buried his face in his hands once more, his phone now abandoned somewhere on the couch. “You knocked his number out of my pocket, Cipher.”

“How dare you accuse me of that?!” Cipher gasped dramatically. “Why would I cut my one and only contact to fame and fortune?!”

“Because you were drunk!” Phainon cried. “If only you just got into the damn car!”

“I cannot believe you were making out with a rockstar.” Hyacine was still in awe as she and Castorice continued to search the social media account on Phainon's phone. “Cas, you sure it's this guy?”

Castorice nodded. “It was him. I can't believe it either.”

“Phainon.” Anaxa sighed in resignation. “You're never going to get this guy's number again.”

“I know that! I know!” Phainon cried once more. Phainon was just getting more frustrated by the minute. “How the hell am I supposed to contact a fucking rockstar?!”

“Easy! Just call the number he gave you!”

Aglaea and Anaxa actually had to hold Phainon back from jumping Cipher this time, and Phainon slumped in their arms with a heavy sigh. “I'm never going to have the chance to talk to that guy again.”

“Aglaea, would you have any contacts who could reach this man?” Castorice turned to Aglaea, who immediately shook her head.

“I don't work for anyone who would have a close connection to a rockstar,” Aglaea explained while still holding onto one of Phainon's arms. She was quite the coveted fashion designer, and she has designed outfits for many high-profile guests. Although Castorice had a good idea, unfortunately, it wasn't enough.

“Phainon.” A sorrowful sigh came from Hyacine as she glanced up from his phone. “There's definitely a chance! You could definitely try to message him on here.”

Phainon immediately dismissed the idea. “There's no way a celebrity is going to respond to me on there.”

“He might not even be running the account,” Anaxa added. “It could be a manager or a publicity employee. With how many followers this guy has, it wouldn't come as a shock to me if someone else was running the account for him.”

Phainon heaved another sigh as Aglaea and Anaxa released him. “I'm never seeing him again.”

“Don't say that!” Hyacine chastised. “Let's go back to the club and try to find the napkin outside! And if not, you can make Cipher owe you!”

“Woah, woah, woah.” Cipher held up her hands in the air. “We don't need to be pointing fingers now.”

“It's all your fault!” Phainon and Hyacine both yelled together.

“Let's just go now,” Castorice suggested. “The sooner we go, the more likely the napkin will still be there, right? I mean, we're all still dressed.”

Everyone glanced around, and it was true. They were all still dressed in last night's attire. It seemed like everyone immediately collapsed upon returning to Phainon's apartment.

“Let's go! Let's go!” With Hyacine’s urging, they all quickly filed out of Phainon's apartment and headed to Aglaea's car in the parking lot. Since there were so many of them, they wouldn't fit in Phainon's car. Fortunately, Aglaea had quite the minivan that would fit them all, and they were soon on their way back to the club.

She parked the car at the curb, at the corner where Cipher had thrown up and blacked out the previous night. As this part of the city was only filled with clubs and bars, nothing was open, which made traffic much more lenient for them, and they arrived in record time. Jumping out of the car, they searched for about half an hour all over the sidewalk, but they all came up empty. All there was in this dirty corner was more irrelevant trash, and Cipher’s puke was, unfortunately, still there.

Phainon sighed heavily, running a tired hand through his hair. “It's not here, guys.”

“I told you I didn't kick it out!” Cipher complained. She was squatting on the floor and flicking the other trash that was around this corner. “Ugh, my head hurts, guys.”

Aglaea pinched the bridge of her nose. “No one told you to drink that much.”

“What's the point of going to the club if you don't black out?!” Cipher jumped to her feet and began wildly waving her arms. “Phainon over here was sucking tongues with some random stranger! Ugh, guys, stop talking so loud, my head hurts.” She clutched her head in an attempt to massage it.

“Why didn't your head hurt before?” Hyacine approached Cipher and also began to massage her temples.

“I was too excited over Phainon knowing a celebrity,” Cipher mumbled with a pout. “We could've all been rich!”

“Yeah, if you didn't knock the napkin out of my pocket.”

“I didn't do it! Ow, my head.”

“At this point, losing a celebrity's number is sounding worse than puking all over the floor and blacking out,” Anaxa murmured while Phainon and Cipher continued to bicker. He was still scanning the floor and trying to see if he could find anything, but all the napkins that were haphazardly thrown onto the sidewalk in this corner had already been looked through by them. Unfortunately, none of them contained the name and number they were looking for.

“Should we ask if the bartender knows him?” Castorice suggested. “If he was hanging out at the bar, maybe they are acquainted? Or, he could be friends with the owner of the club?”

“Cas! That's a good idea!” Tribbie, whom they called over earlier to join them to help search, nodded enthusiastically. She wasn't much of a clubber, so she only had dinner with them last night before parting from them while everyone else went to the club. “It's Saturday, so they will be open late today too.”

“If anything, that guy might be back too,” Anaxa stated. “But I'm not going here again, so find someone else.”

“Didn't like the drinks?” Castorice guessed.

“Too loud.”

Aglaea frowned, turning in Anaxa's direction. “That's literally what a club is.”

“I didn't ask for your opinion.”

She laughed. “When do you ever ask for opinions?”

Anaxa scowled at her words and crossed his arms. “I specifically don't want your opinion.”

It was Anaxa and Aglaea's turn to bicker with each other, and Phainon let out another sigh over their bickering. “Fine, okay, I'll try and come back tonight.”

“I want to come!” Hyacine shot her hand up, and Cipher winced right next to her.

“Stop being so loud! Please!” Cipher wailed once more, and Hyacine quickly began apologizing and massaging her temples once more.

“I can come too.” Castorice offered Phainon a small smile. “Since I've seen him in person as well, I could be a little bit more helpful.”

“I want to come,” Cipher grumbled.

“You're not going.” Aglaea immediately stopped her bickering to chastise Cipher.

“But why?! I want to meet a celebrity!”

“You're hungover, and you want to go to the club again?” It was Aglaea's turn to scowl.

“I'm not carrying you again if you black out.” Phainon joined in. “I might lose something else if I do.

“It wasn't me! The napkin’s not even here! There's no proof I did it!” Cipher cried and immediately grabbed her head once more. “Ow, ow, ow! Guys, can we go back? It's not here, and I want to lay down.”

Phainon heaved another sigh. “I agree. Let's go before I have to carry her again.”

They all dejectedly hopped into Phainon's car once more to return to his apartment. Anaxa, Aglaea, and Tribbie returned home, while Hyacine and Castorice stayed with Phainon to return to the club later that night. Cipher was forcefully dragged home by Aglaea. Even though she swore she wouldn't drink a single drop, she was soon thrown in Aglaea's minivan and was on her way, much to Phainon's relief. He couldn't promise not to jump Cipher the moment Aglaea was not there to protect her.

Phainon, Hyacine, and Castorice didn't do much while they waited for the club to open at 9 PM. They went out to grab some fast food for lunch before returning home, and while they were eating, Hyacine displayed her phone screen onto Phainon's television in the living room.

“I still cannot believe you caught a celebrity’s eye,” Hyacine murmured while scrolling through the social media account once more. Phainon noticed that she had already followed the account, for whatever reason. To his knowledge, Hyacine was not interested in rock music at all.

“I still cannot believe I lost his number.” Phainon released another heavy sigh, lounging on the couch while watching Hyacine click on random posts that caught her eye. She mostly clicked on music videos and concert clips, and damn, he was a good singer. He did sound lovely moaning in Phainon's ears last night, after all, so he wouldn't doubt his singing voice was also just as lovely. He even played guitar; was there anything this guy couldn't do?

“Do you remember, like, any digits at all from his phone number?” Hyacine clicked on a magazine cover, and Castorice's face bloomed red at the sight because Mydei was shirtless on the cover. It was for some luxury clothing brand, which was quite ironic since Mydei was half-naked in the photo.

“Even if I did, they wouldn't help me at all,” Phainon remarked. “What am I going to do? Call every single possible combination of numbers until he answers?”

It was Hyacine's turn to sigh. “I just wish this situation were more… salvageable. If the guy you met was anyone but a famous rockstar with millions of fans, we would have been able to message him on here with no problem.”

“It's whatever.” Phainon continued watching the television screen as flashes of this beautiful, dream man kept appearing. After looking at the social media account for so long, it just made the man he met last night feel more and more like just some drunken dream. Seeing the man performing on stage, starring in music videos, and appearing on magazine covers for high-end brands just made him feel so far away. Should he have even made out with that guy last night? Wouldn't he get in trouble for that as a celebrity? Phainon couldn't fathom what it was like being famous and living such a life.

“It's not just whatever!” Hyacine exclaimed, causing Phainon to jolt in his seat. “Don't you like this guy?! I know you're not the type to have one-night stands, Phainon!”

Phainon settled back down into his seat on the couch, staring back at the post that Hyacine had paused her scrolling on. It was a video of the man sitting on a stool on a stage, playing a slower song on the guitar.

“Of course I'm interested in him,” Phainon murmured, watching the rockstar strum the black guitar in his arms and listening to the microphone in front of him project his smooth singing voice. “But, what could I do? I lost his number, and if no one knows him at the club, then that's it. How else do you contact a celebrity?”

“You could stalk him.”

“Castorice, I'm not going to stalk him.”

“What if, instead of stalking him, you become a super mega fan, get his attention at a concert, and he recognizes you!” Hyacine excitedly squealed. “It'll be just like a movie!”

Phainon tried to imagine that outlandish scenario and frowned. “I doubt he would even remember me by then. And anyway, I don't have a job now that I'm done with pilot school, so I wouldn't be able to afford being a ‘super mega fan.’” With a groan at the reminder, he buried his face in his hands. “Fuck, I have to job hunt now.”

“Don't think about jobs right now! We're focused on this man right now.” Hyacine clicked on another post. It seemed to be some group interview of him and a few others, which Phainon found out from scrolling through his account that they were fellow band members.

“You can only say that because you actually have a job, Hyacine.” Phainon chuckled and glanced her way, but her attention was still focused on the group interview.

“As much as I love my job, Phainon, it's the weekend right now. Stop mentioning work,” Hyacine teasingly chastised him with a smile. Hyacine was a tour guide at the local zoo, and Phainon knew just how much she loved her job. She enjoyed teaching others, entertaining the kids, and spending her day with the other animals. And she was good at her job too, from the few times Phainon had visited her at work.

With a laugh, Phainon and Castorice continued to watch Hyacine scroll through the social media account. They only went out to buy more food for dinner, and then they were on their way back to the club.

There was no line into the club, most likely because it literally just opened its doors for the night, and because it was so early, there was no cover charge either. Phainon, Castorice, and Hyacine were able to quickly enter the club after security had checked Phainon. They darted straight for the bar, but the bartender who was working today wasn't the same as the one from last night. Phainon wasn't sure if there was any hope for him in this venture, but he asked the person working anyway since they had already made the trip to the city's downtown area.

“Mydeimos?” The bartender had to lean forward over the counter to hear what Phainon was saying to her over the thumping music. Thankfully, because the club just opened, they didn't have to yell over the crowds to hear each other like they did last night.

“Do you know him? Or does the owner of the club know him?”

“The rockstar, right? You a fan?” The bartender was cleaning a rocks glass with a towel, and it only served to remind Phainon of the crimson liquid that the man had been drinking from his own glass just the previous night.

“Err, not particularly.” Phainon furrowed his eyebrows. How was he supposed to describe this without sounding like an insane stalker-fan? “I met him last night, but I lost something that he gave me.”

The bartender hummed in acknowledgement, picking up another glass to languidly wipe down. “He does come here sometimes. Maybe you could catch him if you come here often enough. He is a regular here, and we only know him in case we have to step in and stop crazy fans from trying to bombard him. We don't have any means of contacting him, if that's what you were looking for.” She shrugged nonchalantly. “Even if we did, I wouldn't be able to give it to you.”

Phainon nodded. “I see. Thank you.”

“Yeah, good luck on finding him.”

With a nod, Phainon, Castorice, and Hyacine parted from the bar counter. All they were able to learn was that the rockstar was a regular at this club, but he only visited sometimes, which would mean Phainon would just have to randomly visit the club in hopes that he turned up again. It was looking quite bleak for them, but Hyacine and Castorice continued to convince Phainon to visit for the next few weeks in the hopes that he would find the celebrity again. Phainon, who was now accepting the fact that he would never run into him again, obliged nonetheless.

For the next few weeks, Phainon visited the club on Fridays, the same day that he had previously met the rockstar. Sometimes, he even ordered an Old Fashioned just for the sake of it, and it even came to a point where the other bartenders began to recognize him, even referring to him as a regular now. Although it did feel nice having the bartenders ask if he wanted “the usual” for the day, it did not feel nice that the reason he kept visiting the club was just to find a certain individual. However, much to Phainon's luck, he would never run into that man at the club again, and soon, it finally came to a point where Phainon gave up and stopped visiting the club altogether.

chapters.title: Chapter 3: Phainon
chapters.html:
Phainon was in absolute misery. He had been job hunting for the past few months. His routine had been to job hunt and visit the club on Fridays, but now that he had stopped visiting the club a few months ago, he decided to try to forget about the man he met by pouring all his attention into job hunting.

It worked, as he started being offered more interviews over time, the longer he was job hunting and the more he got used to the whole job application process, but he was applying to so many jobs that it was hard to keep track of which jobs he was even applying to. Since he had been out of school for a few months now, he was just desperately applying to anything and everything he was even slightly qualified for. As a result, when he finally received a call back one day, he had no idea what job or company it was for.

Phainon was in the middle of job hunting, as was his daily routine, when his phone began vibrating upon his desk with another random number. It was just the norm for him now to answer calls from strangers in the hopes that it was regarding a job, and it was just another one of those days when he picked up his phone to answer.

“Hello, this is Phainon.” Phainon leaned back in his desk chair, hoping that he didn't just give his name to a spam caller.

“Hello, Phainon, this is Krateros from… Entertainment.”

Phainon furrowed his eyebrows. He did not catch the company name at all, but he tried to sound as excited as he could, nonetheless.

“Hi, Krateros!” If only the man were here to see just how beaming Phainon's work smile was. “How are you?”

The deep voice grunted over the phone. “Good, thank you. I am calling to offer you the position of private pilot for our high-profile client. As I am the client’s manager, I wanted to offer you my congratulations.”

Phainon froze. Woah, he was not expecting a job offer today.

He sat straight up in his chair, running a hand through his hair. Fuck, what was the company name again? Phainon desperately began pulling up his emails to try to find anything with the name “Krateros” in it.

“Wow, thank you so much, Krateros. I truly, sincerely appreciate the offer.” Phainon squinted at his desktop screen as his emails reflected against him. He didn't even have time to be excited as he was still trying to recall who this person was. “It would be great if I could review the details. Would it be possible to send the offer to me in writing so I can get back to you in a couple of days?”

“Of course. I will have the team send it over to you in a few minutes. Please look it over, and I hope to hear some good news from the team.”

With the shortest return offer call ending and with Phainon's heart now pounding in excitement from finally receiving a job offer after so many months of job hunting, Phainon opened up the search bar in his emails. Even though he couldn't even catch the full company name, he searched through his emails nonetheless, searching for “Entertainment” to see if some sort of confirmation email came up from when he submitted his job application. He did remember that the caller's name was “Krateros,” so if all else failed, he could search up that name too. Although there were a few entertainment companies that Phainon had applied to, the only email thread that matched “Entertainment” and “Krateros” was a company named “Kremnos Entertainment.” From the email thread, Phainon gathered that he had passed the initial resume screening, had an interview with their human resources department, had an interview with this man named Krateros, and then he was accepted.

Continuing to squint at his desktop, he tried to recall any possible memory, but to no avail. The email thread was from a few weeks ago, and Phainon could barely even remember what he even had for dinner just last night. He did remember visiting an entertainment company for an interview, and he did remember how awestruck he was at seeing such a grand skyscraper in the city. However, he couldn't really remember anything else.

Kremnos Entertainment? Phainon opened up a search engine in a separate tab and typed the name in. It immediately popped up, and a photo of the building appeared at the top of the search results. It was the exact same skyscraper that Phainon recalled from his memories, and he scrolled down to see if he could find some sort of website that could jog his memory on what his job was even going to be. He could only assume from the job position that he was flying a private jet. Was he flying a private jet for one of the company’s celebrities? Maybe an executive? The man over the phone didn't reveal much at all, and Phainon could only assume that it was classified information until he actually accepted the job offer.

His finger, which was scrolling through the web page, immediately froze when an extremely familiar name was shown to him. Staring at the name, with his heart now pounding for an entirely different reason, he reread it over and over and over again, as if finally receiving a job offer had suddenly made him delusional.

“There's no way.” Swallowing dryly and even with shaking fingers, Phainon clicked the link that was embedded in the name, and there was no denying the blonde man that appeared all over his screen.

Mydeimos was a part of Kremnos Entertainment.

It was a name he had been trying to forget for the past few months. A name that he had been trying to erase from his mind, but was pouring all of this attention and energy into job hunting instead. But here the name was again, as if it were haunting Phainon of his stupid mistake all those months ago. He could barely even remember what the guy sounded like anymore, and it was weird that he could just click on any video of him and hear his voice again.

It was then that he received an email. Phainon quickly clicked on the notification, and it was, indeed, from Kremnos Entertainment. It was an official offer letter with details of his job position, expectations, benefits, and salary. And holy fuck was the salary good. It was honestly a little too good. The benefits were also not bad at all either, and it even came with a hefty sign-on bonus. Phainon was about ready to accept any measly offer that came his way, but perhaps his luck was looking up for him again.

Maybe losing the celebrity's number was the cost he had to pay for receiving such a grand return offer. The only thing the offer letter didn't include, which Phainon would have been surprised if it even was included, was who this “high-profile client” Phainon would be flying around in their private jet.

It didn't matter to Phainon, as this offer was way too good to let down. And, if he managed to run into Mydeimos, that would be even better. In fact, that would be ideal. Even though he was just starting to get over the guy, it was only because he had absolutely zero means of contacting the man. But now, he had a chance again, and a new fire surged within Phainon as he continued rereading the offer letter over and over again and reviewing the benefits multiple times. Phainon wouldn't have expected to be accepted as a private pilot, since he had just recently received all the necessary certifications and pilot hours a few months ago, but he couldn't exactly complain about a job offer.

It was quite the sweet deal as a private pilot. The position promised a schedule a month ahead of time, which was atypical for a private pilot, and Phainon was quite amazed that he could even call out sick in the first place. The position details mentioned that, in the case he needed to call out for any sort of reason, they would call a backup pilot from the company. Which was… quite generous to say the least. And as his position was under the company of Kremnos Entertainment, he was also getting the benefits and job protection of any average employee working at their headquarters rather than an on-call, separate entity that just worked with the company’s clients. That also meant that Phainon could be called upon at any time to fill in for any other private pilots who called out within the company, but Phainon didn't really mind at all. There was only one thing left to do now.

Phainon was now employed.

“Congratulations!”

With resounding cheers echoing across the table, everyone clinked their glasses together, laughing and hollering amongst each other. It was a few days after Phainon had accepted the job offer, and Phainon informed his friends that he was finally employed. It was a Saturday night, and all his friends had gathered at a restaurant in the city to celebrate Phainon's employment over a nice evening dinner. Phainon didn't reveal much to his friends other than that he had accepted a job offer, as he wanted to reveal to them in person what the job was. He was also sure they were going to be flabbergasted at the company he was working for, and he wanted to see their reactions in person.

“You didn't tell us what job you accepted!” Hyacine leaned forward at their table toward Phainon. “I've been waiting all week to hear what job you have now! I was feeding the pandas at work and kept thinking about it all week.”

“We gotta see who gets paid the most now,” Cipher chimed in. “No one is beating Aglaea's fashion designer salary.”

“I only get paid a lot when my designs are used.” Aglaea took a sip of her wine with a light chuckle. “Otherwise, I am making patterns for nothing.”

“Aglaea, you get paid almost millions for your designs!” Cipher cried. “I still remember all the fashion shows you get invited to.”

“That's quite the exaggeration, but thank you, Cipher.” With a smile, she set a delicate hand on Cipher's shoulder to sit her back down, as the woman had jumped up from her seat from excitement at some point over Aglaea's salary.

“Tell us, Snowy! Tell us!” It was Tribbie's turn to jump up and down in her seat, and Phainon laughed at the enthusiasm over his own employment.

“I definitely don't get paid as much as Aglaea does.” With a chuckle, Phainon began pulling up the offer letter on his phone for them.

“Is it a lot though?” Of course, money was the only thing at the front of Cipher's mind.

Another laugh escaped Phainon as he finally located the offer letter in his emails. “It's definitely more than your police officer salary, Cipher.”

“No way!” Before Phainon could turn his phone around, Cipher had already stood up and snatched it from his hands across the table. He blinked blankly at his empty hand before turning to Cipher, who was already scrolling through his phone.

“Holy…” Cipher's eyes were as wide as the plates set in front of them as she continued scrolling through Phainon's phone in her hand. Everyone at the table only watched her with anticipation, waiting to hear what else Cipher had to say.

“So? What's the verdict, Cipher?” Hyacine leaned over the table to try and get a view of the screen, but because she was sitting across from Cipher, and because Cipher was still standing, she couldn't exactly see much.

“The verdict is that Phainon's paying for our dinner tonight!” Cipher threw her hands up into the air. “Phainon, I want three more cocktails! No, make it five! Six! Twelve!”

“I haven't even started yet! And you want twelve cocktails?! Does this place even serve twelve different kinds of cocktails?!”

“Oh, please.” Cipher waved Phainon's cries away. “The moment you get that sign-on bonus, you could pay for everyone’s meal a thousand times over. And, why do you think I'm not going to repeat the good alcohol?”

“You get a sign-on bonus?!” Hyacine exclaimed.

“It must be a big company,” Castorice added. “Where is it?”

They all stared back at Cipher, who still had Phainon's phone in her hands, and she quickly glanced back down at the offer letter. “It's… uh… Kremnos Entertainment?”

“Woah!” Hyacine jumped excitedly up and down in her seat, turning to Phainon, who was seated right beside her. “That's one of the biggest celebrity management companies!”

“Celebrity?!” Phainon swore he could see dollar signs in Cipher's eyes. “No wonder he gets paid so damn much! Maybe I should've gone to pilot school.”

“I would not trust you to drive my plane, Cipher.”

“Aww, Anaxa! I wouldn't want to drive you either!”

“Do not call me that.”

“I've honestly never heard of it before until now.” Phainon chuckled. “I only just looked it up when I received the offer.”

“Ooh, you're right!” Hyacine began digging for her own phone. “We should look up all the celebrities at Kremnos Entertainment.”

“Celebrities?!”

“Yes, Cipher, I work at a famous entertainment company now. You don't have to get excited about it again.”

“I feel like you weren't this excited when you heard about my clients,” Aglaea chimed in with a light laugh.

“Well, that's because that's expected of you, Aglaea!” Cipher truly was Aglaea's biggest fan. “See, I wouldn't expect Phainon to be working with famous people.”

“So why did you say my name like that?”

“You know exactly why I said your name like that.”

“Guys!” A sharp gasp pierced the air, and everyone's attention was now drawn to the pink-haired girl looking down at her phone. It was a dimly-lit restaurant, and the phone screen brightly illuminated Hyacine's shocked expression. “That guy… That–That guy!”

“That guy,” Anaxa deadpanned.

“The guy! The guy that… That guy! Phainon's guy!” Hyacine stammered, staring at everyone with wide eyes. “The… The blondie! The rockstar!”

Phainon only understood what she was saying because he already knew this information, and he was trying really hard not to laugh at how flabbergasted Hyacine was. But he was shocked when Castorice, who was sitting on his other side, gasped along with Hyacine.

“Is he under Kremnos Entertainment?” Castorice had brought a hand up to her mouth to cover her open mouth, and everyone’s eyes went wide when they finally understood what Hyacine was trying to convey.

“Yes! Mydeimos is under Kremnos Entertainment!” She exclaimed and turned her phone screen around. Under a list generated by the search engine that listed well-known names that were being managed by this company, one of them very clearly read “Mydeimos.”

“There's no way!” Cipher, who had just started to get settled in her seat, jumped up once more. “We're going to meet a celebrity! A celebrity!”

“Wait, wait.” Phainon had to raise his hand before she started getting ahead of herself. “I don't know who I'm a private pilot for. It could just be for some executive at the company and no one famous.”

“Aww.” Cipher sank back down to her chair with a pout, and Aglaea laughed, patting her shoulder comfortingly.

“They didn't tell you when you accepted the offer?” Anaxa frowned.

“They told me I would meet them on my first day.

“That's… suspicious.” Anaxa crossed his arms and leaned back in his chair. “They should've told you when you signed the offer letter. Are you sure this place is real?”

“I definitely went there in person to interview,” Phainon explained while Cipher handed Phainon's phone over to Anaxa so that he could also review the offer letter. “I also thought they would tell me after I signed the offer letter, but they just said I would meet them on my first day.”

Anaxa hummed as the phone screen illuminated his face this time. “You really do get paid a lot.”

“Right?!” Cipher jumped up once more, but was quickly pulled down again by Aglaea. “That's why I want twelve cocktails!”

“With this bonus, Phainon could pay for way more than twelve.”

“You really think so, Anaxa?!” Cipher's eyes were glowing even under the dim restaurant lighting.

“I told you to stop calling me that.”

“I'm not buying you twelve cocktails, Cipher!” Phainon sharply cut in.

“But Anaxa said you could buy even more than twelve! If you're not buying me twelve, can you buy me thirty-three?”

“Where the fuck did you get such an exact number from?! And when did you ever agree with Anaxa?!”

“When he said you could buy me more than twelve cocktails!”

“So where did the number thirty-three come from?!”

“It just spoke to me!” Cipher raised the menu sideways and began flapping the cover, imitating a talking mouth. “‘Cipher, order thirty-three cocktails. Phainon will pay for it all.’”

Castorice giggled. “Why does the menu have such a deep voice?”

“That's the sound of me after thirty-three cocktails.” Cipher nodded enthusiastically.

“Why would I get you thirty-three cocktails so your voice could change?” Despite the exasperating situation, Phainon couldn't help but be amused by her antics.

Cipher batted her eyelashes from across the table. “Don't you want me to sound more like your love, Mydeimos?”

“That's–What?!” Phainon's face burned red at the sudden mention of the rockstar. If Phainon was in the middle of drinking anything upon hearing her words, he was positive he would have spit it all over the table. “Why would I want you to sound like him?!”

“Aww, Phainon, I'm sure you miss his voice!” Cipher cooed.

Phainon was sure his red face could be seen even in this darkened restaurant. “Even so, I don't want you to sound like him!”

“Wait.” Cipher suddenly grew rigid. “You think if I actually sounded like him after thirty-three cocktails, I could get signed by Kremnos Entertainment and become the next biggest rockstar?”

“Why are you imagining thirty-three cocktails already?!” Phainon wailed.

“There's only one way to find out!” Tribbie exclaimed, and Phainon couldn't even believe he was watching Cipher and Tribbie high-five each other over Aglaea's head, as Aglaea was sitting in the middle between the two of them.

“Cipher,” Castorice cut in, and Phainon really thought he was saved. That was, until he heard her next words: “That's a great idea for a story.”

Phainon tiredly buried his face in his hands while Cipher began exclaiming, “Right? Right?! You gotta start taking notes and make it the next script you write!”

Cipher and Castorice somehow began brainstorming for this wild story, and Phainon sincerely hoped a new theatrical play wasn't about to be released under Castorice’s name. In the midst of them adding a gay romance into the mix when the main character, whose voice changed after thirty-three cocktails, made out with a suspiciously familiar new graduate at a suspiciously familiar club, Hyacine turned toward Phainon.

“Did you know Mydeimos was under Kremnos Entertainment?” On her phone screen, she still had the list of celebrities open.

Phainon laughed at her question, rereading the man's name on her phone. “I wanted to see everyone’s reactions once you found out. I only found out myself when I received the offer and looked up the company.”

“It's certainly surprising.” Somehow, Aglaea was communicating just fine next to Cipher, who was at some part of the story where the new graduate was begging on their knees for the celebrity to stay by their side. “Will you speak with him if you cross paths with him?”

Determined, Phainon nodded. “I could only hope he gives me the time to explain myself.”

Resting her chin in the palm of her hand, Aglaea tilted her head to the side. “Still, he may not be interested in you anymore. Will you still try to talk to him?”

“Even then, I still want to explain myself. I just want to sort out any misunderstanding about me that he may have had on his end.”

“Even if he doesn't want to speak to you?”

“Even if…” Phainon trailed off. He didn't even think about that. He was so intent on speaking to the rockstar that he hadn't even considered the slightest possibility that he might not even want to see Phainon at all. What did Mydeimos even think of him? Phainon could only hope it was nothing negative, but with the way Phainon had basically ghosted the guy, he was sure there were no positive thoughts about him left in Mydeimos’s head.

“Aglaea!” Hyacine cut in. “Don't say that! We should be rooting for Phainon right now!”

She shrugged. “It's something worth considering. Will you beg for him on your knees to listen to you like what their story is saying?” Aglaea waved a hand toward Cipher, who was still droning on about the story with Castorice.

With a light laugh, Phainon really tried to imagine the hypothetical situation. “If he really didn't want to see me… I think I would try as hard as I could to get him to listen to me, no matter what. He doesn't… have to agree with what I say or start anything with me; I don't have those expectations at all. But, I just hope he will listen to me, even if it's selfish of me to ask for.”

Hyacine pouted. “Phainon, you should be hoping he still wants to date you.”

“Date?!” Phainon immediately blushed once more. “I don't even know if the guy wanted to date me all those months ago!”

“Well, he gave you his number because he was at least interested in you, right?” Hyacine remarked. “Surely, he considered the idea of dating you.”

“I'm sure he did before I practically ghosted the guy.” Phainon sighed.

“It wasn't on purpose!” Hyacine patted Phainon's wilted shoulders. “I'm sure he'd understand.”

Phainon frowned. He really didn't think that hot-tempered guy, who was starting an argument over a stranger’s literal drink order, would peacefully listen to him, but Hyacine had never met the guy to know what he was like. Now that he was thinking back on his temper, he started feeling more and more nervous. There was absolutely no way he wasn't furious with Phainon, right?

Well, Phainon didn't have to worry about that unless he actually met Mydeimos, and surely a rockstar such as him would be busy and booked the entire day, right? Maybe they would never even cross paths at all, even if they were working at the same company.

“It's nice to see you again, Phainon.”

Phainon nodded and shook the hand that was held out in front of him. Now that he was seeing Krateros in person, he definitely remembered the guy. With his dark brown hair, graying bangs that matched his thick mustache and beard, and a scar down one side of his face, Phainon clearly remembered thinking how cool this guy looked. The guy looked like he, himself, was a rockstar.

“It's nice to be here.” Phainon smiled at the older man. Phainon had just come from Kremnos Entertainment’s headquarters to complete onboarding paperwork and orientation, and it was the afternoon by the time Phainon arrived at the city's airport. The human resources team instructed Phainon to meet Krateros there, and true to their word, he was waiting outside the private jet that Phainon would be flying. It was an extremely sleek beauty, this Dassault Falcon 8X, and Phainon could tell the private jet cost a very pretty penny just from looking at it–a pretty penny as in millions of dollars.

“The individual I manage and your co-pilot are already in the jet.” Krateros gestured towards the door. “I'd like for you to inspect the aircraft and anything else you would need to do before we set off for the day. Once you’re finished, I can introduce you to them. The flight attendant will be arriving soon, and I can take your luggage in for you. You received the flight schedule, correct?”

Phainon nodded once more, and Krateros bid him a brief farewell before disappearing into the aircraft. He had received the flight schedule the night before, and he was quite surprised at how many places they were going to. He was basically flying them across the country, hitting every major city along the way, before returning back to their starting point. He couldn't even begin to imagine who he was possibly flying for still.

With the sheer size of this private jet, Phainon wasn't the least bit surprised he had a co-pilot; in fact, he probably would've been more nervous if he didn't have a co-pilot. As Phainon had never flown this specific jet before, he really wanted to do a careful inspection of both the exterior and interior before setting off. Considering how beautiful and almost pristine the condition of the private jet in front of him was, Phainon was sure there wouldn't be much to attend to.

With a sigh, Phainon began his inspection. Like his previous thoughts were saying, there really wasn't much he had to do. Actually, the more he inspected the aircraft, the more it seemed like it was brand new. There were absolutely zero signs of wear, and every single part that Phainon checked over was basically the newest model. Even when he climbed inside the cockpit, it just made Phainon all the more nervous. Was this private jet really brand new? How rich was this company to just afford a brand new jet? He originally thought he was just replacing a private pilot who left a vacancy, but now Phainon was realizing that the company had posted a whole new position.

Everything was basically in top shape, and even the co-pilot had already recorded the predicted weather during their route, so there wasn't much left for Phainon to do. Exiting the cockpit, he found Krateros sitting at the conference table in one of the plush seats to the right side of the aircraft. Considering that the main area was empty, he could only assume that the co-pilot and the person he was flying were all the way in the back of the plane, where the divan was. It was where people on private jets usually slept, since the divan could be converted into a bed.

As he approached Krateros, the man glanced up from his laptop. “Done?”

“Everything looks great. In fact, everything looks really new.” Phainon chuckled as Krateros pushed himself up from his seat.

“Good. It should, since we just bought this plane.”

Phainon’s eyes widened in shock while Krateros began to walk towards the back of the plane. So the aircraft actually was brand new?! He couldn't even comprehend the sheer amount of money this company had, and it still didn't completely settle with him, even while approaching the back of the plane to follow Krateros.

It was quite the swanky private jet with plush seating facing each other right when you exit the kitchen that was in front of the cockpit, more of the same seating to the right, but with a conference table, and a credenza to the left that was also padded on the top so anyone could comfortably use it as a seating bench as well. Toward the back of the plane, which could be accessed through an arched doorway, Phainon could only assume the sleeping area was there, along with the bathroom and storage for their luggage.

Before Krateros could open the door leading to the back of the plane, the entrance to the jet burst open, jolting both Phainon and Krateros.

“I'm here!”

Phainon whirled around towards the source of the loud voice, and there a woman stood in the classic flight attendant uniform, with a button-up, collared dress shirt adorned in a black waistcoat and flared, black dress pants. She must be the flight attendant that Krateros mentioned earlier.

“Empousa,” Krateros’s voice sounded behind Phainon, “this is the new pilot.”

“Oh, hi!” The woman, Empousa, began wheeling her luggage over to their direction. “Yes, Krateros mentioned you before. It's nice to finally meet you.”

With a smile, Phainon laughed at the grand entrance. “It's nice to meet you too. I look forward to working with you.”

“Oh, don't be so formal.” Empousa waved her hand in the air. “We're all friends here, just trying to get to our destination. Has he met everyone yet?”

“We were just about to before you busted into the plane,” Krateros tiredly answered. It seemed that they had already worked together long enough for Krateros to become used to Empousa’s antics.

“Oops!” Empousa laughed. “Sorry, sorry! Let's go then! You're Phainon, right?” She began pushing Phainon with one hand over to the closed door while pulling her luggage behind her. “Our boss is super generous. I'm sure you'll get along with him, no problem!”

“Could you tell me a bit about him?” Phainon stumbled over his feet when he suddenly started getting pushed down the aisle, and he eventually caught himself when they arrived at the door.

“He's quite famous, you know! Maybe you already know about him?”

“I don't even know his name,” Phainon chuckled sheepishly.

“Oh! Krateros didn't tell you yet?” Empousa leered over Phainon's shoulder at the older manager, who only rolled his eyes in response. “If you're into rock music, don't freak out too much.”

“Rock… music?” Phainon swore he felt the pit of his stomach sinking, and his feet would've been rooted to the floor if Empousa hadn't hurriedly pushed him through the door that Krateros had finally opened. There was no way, right? There was genuinely, absolutely, no way it was who he was thinking of, right? He was sure there was more than one rock singer under Kremnos Entertainment, right? One that was much more famous and popular than the man whom Phainon was currently thinking of?

As he stumbled through the door, he was too busy trying to catch himself to properly look at everyone in the room, but he didn't have to.

“Mydei!” Empousa exclaimed, pushing Phainon over by his shoulders. “Come meet the new pilot!”

Wide golden eyes met Phainon’s blue ones, and Phainon froze under his gaze. His entire body grew tense, and he couldn't even breathe, let alone make a single sound. It was only a few months ago, yet it felt like an eternity since he saw that golden head of hair, sharp, cat-like eyes, and chiseled jawline. He was just as intimidatingly attractive as Phainon remembered, and even more attractive than the posts of the man Phainon had seen all over his social media account. It was the same person that had been filling Phainon's mind for months, and it was the same person Phainon could no longer reach to the point where he just had to give up and move on.

That was, until now.

chapters.title: Chapter 4: Mydei
chapters.html:
Mydei had been existing in bed for the past week. He would scroll through his phone, throw it across his bed, and then continue scrolling through his phone for hours and days with no end in sight. He didn't want to do anything, and he didn't want to think about anything at all. Mydei just felt like an empty husk that existed in this bed forever and ever.

It had been a week since he had voluntarily quit his own band. It was a band that was formed when he was young and stupid in school, and it was formed with five of his equally stupid friends. They had grown together as a band from the ground up, playing in janky garages and overcrowded clubs. They had spent days and weeks crowding in each other’s rooms and overstuffed closets, writing music, and recording songs before eventually landing their first official contract with Kremnoan Entertainment when they were offered a business card at one of their many lousy concerts in some underground club. They went from an old garage to an official recording studio, but all they wanted was to just play music together. That was the only plan that they had; no one had ever expected to make a full-time career out of it, let alone face all the pressure that came from being a celebrity.

He had a disagreement with his bandmates. Mydei wanted to make new music. They had been writing the same old stuff for so many years, and Mydei wanted to try something new. He wanted to push the band into a new direction, and he wanted to foster growth within the band, their music, and themselves. Mydei wanted to explore new things, to try new things, and to put the band out of its comfort zone. He thought it would be good for everyone, and he still believed that even now. His bandmates, however, wanted to stay true to their roots. It was something that Mydei could understand, as that was where they came from and how they got to where they were now. Although Mydei did care about their fans, he cared more about his passion for music, and even if there was a possibility their fans wouldn't like their new stuff, Mydei still wanted to go for it. Nonetheless, his bandmates overruled him, so Mydei could do nothing but continue in the same direction as before.

Their disagreement got in the way of everything. It got in the way of Mydei's singing to the point that even news outlets were reporting on his voice. It affected his songwriting, and even interviewers were urging them with answers as to why their lyrics were not the same anymore. It affected their stage performance, and fans wondered why Mydei didn't have nearly as much energy on stage anymore. Social media was a poison, and it constantly speculated what happened to him; injuries that didn't exist, family problems, even though Mydei was now estranged from his parents, overworking even though Mydei was well-rested, and mismanagement that didn't exist in Kremnos Entertainment. Everything and anything that was on camera was heavily scrutinized, and fans and media outlets were making up reason after reason for Mydei’s shift in behavior.

His bandmates kept urging him, but Mydei couldn't truly change how he felt. They knew how many eyes were on them and how much pressure the public was pushing onto them, but Mydei still couldn't help his emotions. It left him stressed and destroyed, and he couldn't even be a good lover to Hephaestion, the drummer of their band. They got into so many arguments over the band, over Mydei’s performance, and over themselves. It ruined Mydei's heart to continue staying with the band, and even after trying so hard, Mydei made the decision to leave. He knew best how he felt, and he was the harshest critic of himself and hated his performance the most. Despite his bandmates wanting him to stay, their differences in the band's direction would eventually tear them all apart, so Mydei decided to leave first. He broke up with Hephaestion, broke up with the band, and left for good. He had even tried to leave Kremnos Entertainment altogether about a week ago, but the CEO had a different idea for Mydei: To go solo.

Mydei had never considered the idea of going solo at all. He only came this far because he just wanted to make music with his friends; he couldn't ever imagine doing it all by himself. It had been a week since the idea was proposed to him, and he was still tossing and turning in bed. The news of his leaving the band, The Detachment, hadn't been made public yet, but Mydei couldn't help but continually search through social media to see if anyone had caught on. The entertainment company’s public relations department was truly an expert, because even after a week, no news had escaped at all.

With a loud sigh and another throw of his phone, Mydei pushed himself off from his bed. He needed to get out of this Hellhole before his brain exploded. He had been cooped up in his room for the entire week thinking about the band, his old friends and bandmates, his ex-boyfriend, and going solo. Mydei wanted to forget about it all and think about literally anything else. And where was the best place to go to forget all about your problems? There was obviously only one place to go, and Mydei pulled a simple outfit over his body before venturing out of his door.

Mydei thanked the bartender over the pounding music, taking a mighty sip of his pomegranate cocktail. He had left his phone at home, not only to forget about his problems, but also so that his manager wouldn't find him sneaking out to the club when Mydei was supposed to be lying low from the public. His manager, Krateros, was the manager for the entire band, and they had put their activities on pause while Mydei’s exit from the band was finalized. Because of that, they were inactive on every platform, and the public was wondering what happened to them. Krateros had instructed him to lie low, but Mydei was going to lose his mind if he did that. So here he was, at a club that he hadn't been to in quite a long time, sipping on a cocktail in hopes of forgetting all about his problems.

He used to come here quite often with his bandmates, but once they had become so well-renowned, they hadn't come here to avoid attracting attention. It was nice seeing that basically nothing had changed since all those years ago when he and his friends would get blackout drunk and do only God knows what.

Mydei clicked his tongue in annoyance. He came here specifically to forget about everything and everyone. His plan was to get so blasted that he would even forget his name. Mydei wanted to drink the night away, dance the night away, and hear Krateros’s scolding tomorrow while he was hungover. That was the night's plan, and Mydei was on his third cocktail when someone next to him had ordered an Old Fashioned.

Mydei scowled. Who the Hell is ordering whiskey at a club?

“You're actually ordering that?” Mydei almost wanted to believe the guy was ordering it as a joke, and he was even waiting for the man to change his drink order

“Excuse me?” The stranger glared in his direction. Oh fuck; the guy had actually heard him over the music and people? Mydei couldn't help his tipsy brain from verbalizing his thoughts, but he didn't think it would be a problem since it was so deafeningly loud in the club.

“That. You're willingly going to drink that?”

“Do I know you?!”

Obviously not, but Mydei still found it amusing that the man was even entertaining this conversation with a stranger. If someone had mocked his order, he would've just left. Mydei was surprised the guy was even still talking to him.

“Does anyone know anyone else at this club?”

“If you don't know anyone, then why judge what I'm drinking?”

Mydei wanted to laugh at the situation. He hadn't meant to actually be heard by the guy, yet here he was, getting into an argument with some stranger at the club. Would Krateros have to pull him out of a fistfight tonight? Krateros was never going to let Mydei out of his sight ever again if “laying low” somehow became “get into an argument with some stranger at the club over his weird drink choice and eventually start throwing fists.”

“I'm only judging because who the fuck orders an Old Fashioned at a club?”

“What's wrong with an Old Fashioned?!”

Was this guy seriously asking that question? Did this man just burn all his taste buds away from drinking so much whiskey? “It's bitter as Hell.”

“Then what the fuck are you drinking?!”

His question suddenly reminded him of the actually good drink in front of him. With a smirk, Mydei lifted the glass from the counter. “It's definitely way better than an Old Fashioned.”

While locking eyes with the stranger, he downed the majority of his drink, reveling in that sweet taste of pomegranate that washed over his entire being. It was a taste that he would never get tired of, and it definitely beat out any drink with whiskey in it. It seemed that even the stranger was intrigued, as he didn't move a muscle even when the bartender had placed his Old Fashioned on the counter next to them.

“Give that to me.” The man held out his hand.
