“That's what I said.”

Krateros threw the phone back onto Mydei's mattress. “I'm surprised.”

“Surprised about what?” A dry laugh left Mydei's lips. “That I'm taking my career seriously?”

A loud scoff escaped Krateros, and he took a huge gulp of his soda. “As much as you care about your work, you still do whatever the fuck you want. So what happened? You obviously like the guy if you keep sitting here and stalking him.”

“It's not stalking.”

“The Hell do you call this, then? Scrolling endlessly on this man's account, who you don't even talk to?”

Mydei could not answer his question.

“So what happened?” Krateros repeated.

It was as if the entire night replayed in Mydei's mind, and his eyes wavered at the thought of Phainon once more. “Nothing happened. That's the whole problem.”

Krateros fell silent, staring at Mydei as if he were mentally receiving an entire recount of Mydei's life, starting with his night at the club, which Mydei really hoped Krateros couldn't actually see. All he did was pick a fight with a stranger, make out with said stranger, and finger himself to that stranger for the past twelve days.

“So he ghosted you.”

That made Mydei pause. Did he actually just see a recount of Mydei's past two weeks? He really fucking hoped not.

At Mydei's silence, Krateros ran a tired hand through his dark brown hair. “How surprising. That guy didn't give me that impression.”

“Yeah, well.” Mydei could only shrug. “Men.”

Krateros heartily laughed, raising his can of soda to that before downing the rest of his drink. Krateros was definitely a very straight man, but even he appreciated a good joke with a good drink.

With that laugh, Mydei began indulging in the food that Krateros had brought for him. It was seasoned chicken wings that were lavished in a rich and creamy sauce, and they were surprisingly still somewhat warm. Taking a bite into the tangy sauce that drenched the meat made Mydei realize just how starving he was.

“So now what? You going to sit here mourning the man of your dreams?” Krateros set the empty can down onto the floor and learned right back into the chair, kicking his feet upon Mydei's bed. “Or are you going to pour all of that into your work instead?”

Mydei scoffed at that, ripping another tender piece of the chicken. “What do you think, Krateros, of me going solo?”

“I think you would be great at it,” Krateros answered, stealing a chicken wing. Was it really stealing if Krateros paid for it? “I was relieved when the company told me they made you that offer. I thought it would be a waste for someone of your talents to leave, and I figure the company thinks that as well. Out of The Detachment, you're the member with the most fans. You'll do just fine without your bandmates, and the band can adjust without you.”

Flashes of old memories with the band ran through Mydei’s mind, and he smiled solemnly, tearing his teeth back into his food. “That means I'll have to get a new manager.”

Krateros paused in his bite. “What are you talking about?”

Mydei appeared equally as confused. “Because you're the manager for the band?” Mydei thought this was obvious knowledge. “You can't manage two talents at once.”

“I'm leaving.”

The bite of food lodged in Mydei's throat, and he choked on his food. With a laugh, Krateros reached down and cracked open another can of soda, handing it over to Mydei, who downed the carbonated drink. Where was Krateros pulling all this soda from?

Gasping for breath, Mydei finally readjusted with Krateros patting his back.

“You're what?”

“I'm leaving The Detachment.”

Mydei narrowed his eyes, gripping tightly onto the can in his hand. “For what? Just because I'm leaving doesn't mean you have to.”

Krateros laughed, withdrawing his hand from Mydei's back. “What difference does it make, whether I manage you or The Detachment?”

“Then you can just stay with The Detachment. Why bother going through the trouble of leaving?”

“I enjoy managing you more than I enjoy managing The Detachment.”

That truly made Mydei pause once more. Did his ears actually hear that, or was his mind just imagining nonsensical things now? That was the nicest thing Krateros had ever said to him in all these years of Krateros being his manager. Was he dying tomorrow?

He quickly gathered himself after getting over his initial daze. “So if I go solo, you're leaving The Detachment to be my manager?”

“That's right.”

Mydei couldn't help the laugh that slipped past his lips and took another sip of his soda. Damn, now he was wishing this was a beer. “So, you and I will both be leaving The Detachment?”

Krateros smirked and plucked another chicken wing from the open to-go container. “Only if you go solo.”

Returning the smirk, Mydei tossed the idea in his head. If both the company and his manager thought it was a good idea, then why shouldn't he? Why hesitate? Who needed Phainon anyway? He was rich and famous, and he should be enjoying a life all to himself, making music and performing in front of millions of people. Meeting new people, pouring his soul into music–that was his life. Why was he wasting his time away in bed, thinking about a man who wasn't going to give him the time of day?

“Fine. Schedule me a meeting with the executives.”

Mydei was going to show that bastard who ghosted him that he didn't need him at all. That stupid and handsome silver-haired bastard who was way too good at using his tongue, how dare he have the audacity to ghost Mydeimos, the biggest rockstar of the current century?

A few weeks had passed since that conversation with his manager, and it was during that same week he had that conversation that Mydei spoke with the executives at his company. It was official: Mydeimos would be debuting as a solo artist, and Krateros would be his manager. The Detachment would be assigned a new manager. News of Mydei's drop from the band still hadn't been made public yet, and only circulated within the company, yet now that so many more people knew, it was clear that rumors were already circulating within the media. The company decided to drop the official news once Mydei was close to being ready to debut, which would be once a new debut album, complete with a new debut music video, was finalized.

Mydei had been spending the last few weeks holed up in his room, but it wasn't because of the band or that silver-haired bastard anymore. Guitars were strewn all over his bed, and sheet music littered the floors. He had been writing songs with extreme fervor, and after everything that he had experienced a few weeks ago, he had a lot he wanted to say and a lot he wanted to express. There were songs with anger, songs with passion, and songs filled with remorse and regret. One particular song was made that was a lot different from what he usually wrote, and it was the song that the company wanted to choose to be at the top of the track list and made into a music video. They wanted to showcase that Mydeimos was different from The Detachment, and this song would signal his new rebirth.

It was a song of yearning, a song that was made when he reflected on those twelve days. He had officially named it Twelve Days, and although he didn't include the number of times he had masturbated during that period, he included everything else that he felt. He felt loved, and he felt betrayed. He felt anger, yet he felt okay. He felt stupid and dumb, but that's what it was like being young, and that's what he wrote about. The song came to him so easily, and he had never written a song quite like that before with so little effort on his end. Was it weird to be writing a song about a stranger who had ghosted him after only thirty minutes of knowing him? Probably, but it somehow became Mydei's best work.

Only he and Krateros understood what those twelve days truly meant to him, and Mydei still wanted to keep it that way. He left the song as vague in its details as possible, yet as filled with emotion as possible. And somehow, the executives loved it too. They said the vagueness made it relatable to everyone, and the raw emotion they felt from the song brought tears to their eyes. Mydei almost wanted to roll his eyes at how dramatic they were being, but all that really mattered was that they liked the song.

The next few months went by in a blur. Mydei and Krateros were the busiest they had ever felt in preparing for this new debut. Krateros was busy with the logistics: preparing the projected schedule, including scheduling media interviews; interviewing and hiring new staff to assist with supporting a new talent with the agency; buying required supplies and equipment; and coordinating with different studios for song recordings, photoshoots, and music videos, all the while keeping this new solo debut as classified information. Mydei truly, sincerely appreciated Krateros's hard work, and he knew the manager was just as anxious for this solo debut as Mydei was.

Meanwhile, Mydei was trying to churn out all of these songs, and he had to learn and adjust to how to make music without his bandmates. It was hard to get used to; he didn't have anyone to rely on except for the producers within the company who worked with all the talents under Kremnos Entertainment. Considering that his songs were so full of his own emotions, he didn't want to rely too heavily on paid staff employees, but he also didn't have his friends anymore that he could rely on. No one could help him develop a new beat of rhythm, no one could help him write the lyrics. It was all on him now, and it was something that he had to accept now that he was debuting as a solo artist. This was going to be his new life now.

It was later that year, when news of Mydeimos took the world by storm, that he had decided to leave The Detachment voluntarily to debut as a solo artist. Mydei watched the news in real time, seeing all the different theories as to why Mydei decided to leave. Fans referenced Mydei’s latest performances with The Detachment and mentioned how tired and exhausted he seemed; other people argued that he may have had a disagreement with the band. Some others theorized that Mydeimos never got along with his bandmates in the first place and was finally fed up with them. Other people wondered if Mydeimos's contract with The Detachment was finally coming to an end, and he left the moment the contract ended so he could make music on his own now. Because Mydeimos was staying with the company, the company was still held in quite a good standing since the rockstar decided to stay, but many were still angry that they didn't have good enough management to keep The Detachment together in the first place, and that it had to come to Mydeimos leaving for good.

After the news had dropped, there were only a few weeks left until the projected date of Mydeimos’s debut. The songs had already been finished and perfected in the recording studio, the music video was in the midst of finishing its final editing touches, and the photoshoots were already completed. Mydei was getting more and more nervous as the date quickly approached, and he wasn't sure how exactly the public was going to react to his new music. Would they hate his new sound? Mydei felt that it was the typical pattern for fans to hate the new music, as they had become fans due to their old sound. But Mydei wasn't worried too much about that; The Detachment was still making their own music and carrying on their old sound. It just didn't have Mydei’s touch anymore.

Although Mydeimos was a huge rockstar well-renowned across the country, it was still hard to predict just how big his debut would be received. There were both angry fans and excited fans, but what would really be the deciding factor was how they received Mydeimos’s new music in the first place. The executives, although they promised to continue Mydei with his new solo career, no matter how well or poorly it was received, decided they would invest further money depending on the media’s opinion of his songs. This meant that further music videos could be put into production, more interviews could be scheduled, another album could start being written, and even a tour could happen, depending on the public's opinion of Mydeimos. They only invested enough for the basics for now: photoshoots, a music video, one album, and only a handful of interviews, so Mydei could promote his new debut. Everything else would have to wait until after his new album dropped.

There were only four people in his penthouse apartment when it came time for his debut, and Mydei was included in that count. The other people were Krateros, his manager; Empousa, his flight attendant; and Herklas, one of his pilots. They were part of the private jet that flew The Detachment around, and although they still assisted in those flights, they still wanted to come over during Mydei’s date of debut to support him. Mydei and his bandmates had become quite close to these two during the years of flying for their concerts and world tours, and he was plenty grateful that they had come to visit him to support his debut. He had originally thought it would just be him and Krateros in his apartment, watching public opinion spread once the album dropped.

Mydei was nervous, bouncing his leg and watching the countdown of his album's release on his television screen in the living room. He didn't really concern himself with public opinion all too much, but it felt like this was quite the turning point in his career, and whatever the media said about his new album felt like it would portray whether leaving The Detachment was even a good idea or not.

Empousa and Herklas had brought a massive amount of food and alcohol to watch the new music video once it dropped, as Mydei hadn't even seen the music video in its finalized form either, and they were all crowded upon Mydei’s couch, indulging in the food and waiting for the music video to start. Mydei, however, was way too anxious to feel like eating, which didn't escape any of the other three's eyes.

“Mydei, eat.” Empousa threw a container filled with fried chicken on the table, and it somehow landed with perfect accuracy right in front of where Mydei was sitting. “I know you're nervous, but at least fill your stomach with something while we wait.”

“I will throw it up,” Mydei blatantly replied, scrutinizing the fried chicken that glistened under the lights.

The woman sighed and picked at her own chicken drumstick in her hand. “What are you so nervous about? You already played your album to me, and I think it sounds great.”

“She's right.” Krateros's mouth was filled with chicken, and Mydei barely understood what he was saying. “Eat, Mydeimos, and worry after your stomach is filled with good food.”

Mydei sighed and ran a tired hand down his face. It was basically almost midnight, and they were waiting for it to be midnight so that the debut album would drop. But after running around and working overtime for so many months to get everything ready in time for this specific date, he was about to collapse from exhaustion. He was already on his fourth beer, trying to stay awake, but of course, the alcohol was making him even more tired. He was feeling an extreme mix of both exhaustion and anxiety, and Mydei just wanted to fall asleep to not have to feel anything at all.

“Eat!”

The rockstar was jolted awake when a seasoned fried chicken wing was shoved against his mouth, and he had to throw out his arms to stop Empousa from pushing him down.

“The Hell?!”

“I'm not going to stop until you open your mouth!”

A piece of the chicken managed to slip past his parted mouth while he was speaking, and Empousa applauded while Mydei begrudgingly chewed on the meat.

Mydei gulped down the food; he had to admit that it was actually really good with the booze. “My manager is right there, you know.”

“And this was actually your manager's idea.” With a pleasant smile, Empousa sat right back down in her seat and continued to eat. Mydei shot a glare toward Krateros, who refused to lock eyes with the rockstar and kept his head low instead to nibble at his own food. She looked way too pleased with harassing Mydei.

It was then that a loud guitar strum echoed across the living room, and everyone’s attention shot up to the television screen that was now playing the music video. It was starting with a close-up shot of Mydeimos's fingers, playing the guitar to the opening beats of his debut song.

It was midnight.

chapters.title: Chapter 6: Mydei
chapters.html:
The debut was an overall success, much to Mydei's pleasant surprise. Although there was a good part of the media that couldn't get accustomed to Mydeimos's new sound and harshly critiqued his songs, the majority of the media was excited about where Mydeimos would head next. He could tell that promotions for his debut were off the charts, as the number of views on his music video and streams on music streaming services were record-breaking for him.

Mydei took pride in his debut; he had put a lot of effort into the songs and recordings, pushing that silver-haired bastard out of his mind and putting all his attention and energy into working for this debut. The music video came out great, the photoshoots came out nice, and the quality of the song recordings that were being streamed was of high quality, even to Mydei’s picky ears. The executives applauded him and even announced that they would like to do a tour, if Mydei was willing to have one.

Of course, he wanted to have one. What kind of question was that? The best part of being a rockstar, other than being able to create music, was to perform said music. Mydei happily accepted the offer for a tour, and the locations and dates were soon announced. They kept the locations within the country for now, but depending on ticket sales, they may expand to accommodate more dates and locations even outside the country.

Although The Detachment wasn't going on tour, Mydei figured that he would just be using the same private jet that they used to use; however, Krateros had somehow successfully argued with upper management to fund a brand new private jet just for Mydeimos. He was shocked that the approval actually went through, and Krateros had the human resources team quickly push through a new position for another pilot, as the private jet Krateros picked out was huge and required two co-pilots to drive the plane.

Krateros was hustling, and Mydei was plenty amused with the enthusiasm that he held for Mydeimos's solo debut. He worked out the concert venues, ticketing prices, and promotions with the other internal teams for the next few weeks until finally, the tour had arrived. Although the first location of the tour was in the city he already resided in, he would have to fly to the next tour location. Krateros informed him that he and the team had already interviewed and hired a new pilot to work alongside Herklas, and Mydei wouldn't have to worry about a thing except for preparing for his debut tour. Mydei would meet him once they fly was all he was told about the new pilot.

The first day of the tour was a success. Mydei was surprised at how many people even showed up to the concert, and although it was plenty strange performing without his bandmates at his side, it wasn't too bad with all the practicing that Mydei had been putting into preparing for the concert. Considering the positive reception he was hearing after the concert had ended, both from staff, his manager, and social media, he figured he was doing a good enough job. He only had a single day to fly to his next location, and the next concert would immediately take place the day after.

As much as he wanted to collapse into his bed after the concert, he needed to pack since the flight was tomorrow. The styling team usually packed his stage outfits for him, so all he really needed to worry about in terms of clothes was just clothing to sleep in or clothing on the days he had a break. Mydei haphazardly threw in some random shirts, tanks, jeans, and sweatpants, making sure to also pack workout clothes in the case he had time on his rest days to fit in his usual workout routine. In a half-conscious daze, he finished packing the rest of his toiletries, accessories, and other random, miscellaneous items that he wanted to bring with him, as he wouldn’t return home until the tour was over. He also carefully packed his precious guitar, a black custom Fender guitar, with him for the tour. It was his signature guitar that he was always seen with, to the point that even the media itself associated black Fender guitars with the rockstar, Mydeimos.

The rest of the night and his morning were a blur. He finished packing everything, slept through the night, woke up in the morning, and prepared for his flight that was supposed to take up the majority of his day. Krateros picked him up and drove him to the airport, where the new private jet was already waiting for their arrival. They would fly out in the afternoon because the new pilot had to wrap up onboarding and orientation with the company in the morning before heading straight to the airport to fly Mydei. Mydei couldn’t help but frown at that explanation Krateros had given him while they were heading for the airport. What a wild first day for a new hire.

They were waiting in the private jet, which Mydei had already taken the time to admire since it was so brand new, before resting in the back area of the plane with Herklas. Empousa had already messaged Krateros that she was on her way, but there was no rush since they couldn’t exactly leave without the new pilot anyway. Mydei had tried to ask Herklas for any information about the pilot, just to satisfy his own curiosity, but Herklas informed him that he had never met the new pilot either. The human resources team and Krateros were the only people who met the new pilot. Oh well, Mydei wasn’t going to concern himself so much with someone else. He only asked just because.

Krateros was busy working on his laptop in the main area of the private jet, and Herklas was in the back of the plane with Mydei keeping him company. They had already stored all of their belongings away, and Mydei was now relaxing, scrolling languidly through his phone while waiting for takeoff. This was probably the first time in such a long time that he was able to relax, as he was either rushing to finish songs, rushing to shooting locations and studios, or being riddled with anxiety over his debut. Today was a day when he could finally rest now that he knew everything was looking up for him, and he hoped that his luck would stay exactly like that.

Except for the part where Mydei spoke way too soon. The saying “the calm before the storm” rang terribly true for Mydei.

Mydei and Herklas jumped in place when the plane door slammed open. Because the area Herklas and Mydei were in was enclosed by a door, they couldn’t exactly see anything. They had only faintly heard Krateros talking through the closed door, and Mydei wasn’t sure if he was speaking to other people on the phone or if the new pilot had finally arrived. But now, with the door slammed open and a loud, female voice yelling away, Mydei could only assume that Empousa had arrived.

“Looks like Empousa is here,” Herklas muttered without even glancing up from his phone. Both of them were quite used to Empousa’s antics after working with her for so long now.

With a chuckle of agreement, Mydei resumed scrolling on his phone. It was typical Empousa behavior to be late and very loud about it. He wasn’t sure how Empousa managed being a flight attendant without missing a single flight.

He could hear voices talking from beyond the closed door: a mix of Empousa’s voice, Krateros’s voice, and a new male voice, which Mydei could only assume belonged to the new pilot. It meant that everyone was now here for the flight, which also meant they would be taking off soon. As it was early afternoon, it was exactly the time that they had planned on the schedule to depart from the airport. Good job for arriving barely on time, Empousa.

Loud footsteps could be heard in front of the door; what was Empousa doing to that poor new hire out there? But just a few moments later, the door was swung open, and Mydei glanced up and found Krateros.

Even though he couldn’t see Empousa, he could definitely hear her voice ringing from behind his manager: “Mydei! Come meet the new pilot!”

A man dressed in the typical pilot uniform of black slacks, black dress shoes, a white button-up dress shirt that was rolled up to his sleeves, and a black tie was roughly pushed into the area where Mydei and Herklas resided. Why did it feel like Empousa was hazing this new employee? It really wasn’t necessary to push the poor guy over here–

Wait, Mydei was going to immediately take back that previous statement.

The man raised his gaze from the floor after stumbling into the room, and both men widened their eyes at the person before them. Mydei’s shoulders immediately grew rigid at those familiar blue eyes that had haunted him in his sleep, that silver hair that he had pulled on before, and those same lips that Mydei had craved all those months ago.

It was this fucking bastard!

He almost wanted to stand up and just leave the room, but this was his private jet for his tour. Mydei couldn’t even hire a new pilot even if he wanted to, or else he would be way behind schedule and miss a majority of his concert dates. Maybe Herklas could fly the plane himself? No, that was illegal.

“This is Phainon!” Empousa didn’t notice either of the men’s reactions upon laying eyes on each other. “He’s going to be working with Herklas in the cockpit.”

Herklas, who had clearly noticed how uncomfortable Mydei appeared, turned his attention toward Phainon and nodded. “It’s nice to work with you.”

“It’s… nice to work with you too.” It was a rough smile, but Phainon got over his stupor and turned his attention to Herklas. Mydei couldn’t believe it was the same bastard who had ghosted him a few months ago; he was pretty much the only reason Mydei even had a successful debut in the first place.

Phainon glanced at Mydei and winced at Mydei’s not-so-happy expression. “It’s… um… nice to work with you as well, Mydeimos.”

“Oh!” Empousa exclaimed, jumping up and down. “You already know him? You like his music?”

“I… guess so.” A sheepish chuckle left Phainon’s lips. Fuck, he still sounded just as pleasant as ever to Mydei’s ears.

“Do your best,” Mydei only said, and the pilot flinched once more.

“Mydeimos?” Phainon was shaking just like a little puppy. At least he knew he was in the wrong, which made Mydei feel slightly better about himself. “Could we talk?”

“Could you drive the plane now?”

A silence immediately followed Mydei’s words. Even Empousa didn’t know how to react, and her mouth dropped open in complete shock.

Mydei only crossed his arms and turned his head to the side. He wanted to talk now? After leaving him without a single word for all these months? If Phainon wanted him so bad, he should’ve reached out to Mydei while he still had the chance. “We have to leave now if we want to be on schedule.”

“It’ll be quick–”

“Maybe if you drive the plane fast enough, you can come talk to me.”

Another silence followed Mydei’s words. Krateros stared back and forth between the two men, confused as to why Mydei was treating this guy with such hostility, but his eyes suddenly widened in shock as the realization dawned on him. Yeah, he'd better fucking remember the pilot now. Seriously, Krateros interviewed the guy and didn’t even recognize him?

“You a pilot now?” Mydei raised an eyebrow, his glare never ceasing.

“I… yes.” Phainon awkwardly shifted in his spot.

“Great. Show me how well you can fly this thing.”

As if getting the message, Phainon silently and dejectedly left the back of the plane. As much as Mydei felt bad at seeing how defeated the man looked, he still couldn’t forget how abandoned and betrayed he felt waiting for the damn guy to contact him. Not even a single word from him, and here he was, begging to talk to him? As if Mydei was going to give him the time of day.

Three pairs of eyes immediately turned to Mydei.

“Mydei.” Empousa furrowed his eyebrows. “Phainon is a nice guy! Why did you–”

Krateros held his hand in front of Empousa. “Start preparing the kitchen. We will begin takeoff soon.”

Her eyes widened, but she gritted her teeth and stomped out of the room, calling after Phainon. Herklas, getting the silent message that was hanging in the room, nodded and left toward the cockpit to get ready for takeoff as well. He shut the door behind him, leaving both Krateros and Mydei alone to themselves.

“Mydei–”

“You don't have to explain yourself,” Mydei immediately cut him off. He knew Krateros well enough to know he wouldn't have hired him if he remembered that silver-haired man he had seen on his phone screen. “It was an honest mistake.”

“Do you want me to fire him?”

Mydei shook his head. “We won't make the tour in time if we fire him right now.”

“Do you want me to fire him after the tour is over?”

His heart throbbed in his chest, and he scowled. Seriously, even after all these months devoted to forgetting about this guy, his heart still craved him so badly?

Mydei opened his mouth before he could fully stop himself. “It's fine.”

“Mydei–”

“He probably…” Mydei clicked his tongue in frustration, and his eyes wavered. Anyone knew the job market sucked right now, and Mydei felt bad for kicking the guy to the curb after finally landing a job. Phainon probably didn't even know the client he was flying was Mydei in the first place. “You didn't tell him during the hiring process that he was flying for me, right?”

It was Krateros’s turn to shake his head. “I didn't tell him anything until he saw you just now.”

“I figured.” With a deep sigh, Mydei threw his head back, shutting his eyes. “Just keep him. I'll keep it professional moving forward.”

Krateros nodded. “If anything, just let me know.”

It was Krateros's turn to exit the room, and over the speakers, Herklas's voice came through: “It is 63 degrees Fahrenheit and 17 degrees Celsius with sparse clouds in… City. We will be flying for approximately five hours toward… arriving at seven in the evening. Thank you, and we will be taking off soon.”

The engines of the private jet roared as the plane came to life, and Mydei could feel the wheels rolling along the runway to get into position. Watching out the window next to him, Mydei couldn't help but wonder who was currently driving the plane at the moment. Was it Herklas who made the announcement, or did he leave the driving to Phainon? Was he currently watching Phainon at work at this very moment? Considering that he had called him “Mydeimos” rather than “Mydei,” which was the name he had written on his cocktail napkin, Mydei could only assume that Phainon figured out who he was.

Sitting in silence all to himself, with only the roaring engines to fill his ears, Mydei's mind swirled with curiosity, wondering what Phainon wanted to say to him. How was he going to explain himself? Was he finally about to tell Mydei that he was no longer interested? Or was there a certain emergency that had happened that prevented Phainon from ever reaching out to him? Mydei would only forgive him if there was truly some extremely extenuating circumstance that prevented Phainon from contacting him, and even then, Mydei wasn't sure if he could treat him the same as he did a few months ago. Why should he give Phainon the time to explain himself? It was just selfish of him to even want to talk to him after leaving Mydei without a word for so long.

After a few minutes, he felt the plane tilt upward as they all soared into the sky. Mydei watched the city disappear underneath them and be replaced with clouds, and in just a few moments of soaring in the vast open sky, the speakers in the plane went off once more:

“This is Herklas. You are free to get out of your seats now. We are on track toward our destination… Thank you.”

The door to Mydei’s humble room busted open, and Empousa stomped inside as if she were quite literally waiting outside for Herklas's announcement to go off.

Trailing the flight attendant with sharp golden eyes, he watched her mumble and grumble under her breath, slamming the door shut, pouring him his usual mocha coffee, and practically throwing it toward Mydei.

“So,” Empousa huffed and dropped down on the divan right next to Mydei. “What was that?”

“It's mocha coffee.”

“You–!” Empousa looked ready to tear her hair out of her own scalp, but Mydei continued drinking from the coffee cup. “Why did you react to Phainon like that? Do you know him?”

Mydei didn't want to answer that question, as the innocent question had such a messy answer, so he asked her a question instead. “What did he tell you when you chased after him?”

“Nothing!” Empousa threw her hands up into the air and almost knocked the cup right out of Mydei's hands. “Oh fuck, sorry. Phainon didn't tell me anything!”

He furrowed his eyebrows. “He just walked away?”

“He gave me the saddest, most pitiful eyes I had ever seen, smiled, and then sat down in his seat in the cockpit.” Empousa slapped her forehead against her knees. “The fuck did you do to him?! He looked ready to cry!”

“I didn't do anything,” Mydei snapped. “Why are you assuming it was me who did something to him?”

“You gonna make a new hire cry on his first day?!”

“Mydei!”

Mydei continued to ignore Empousa’s exclamations, sipping his coffee instead while she sighed and groaned exasperatedly.

“Okay, fine, whatever.” She waved her hand in the air nonchalantly. “So what did Phainon do to you? I doubt that nice man did anything remotely bad enough to warrant how you treated him just now.”

He raised an eyebrow. “Why do you have zero faith in me?”

“Because Phainon is just a cute little boy on his first day at work!” Empousa jumped up to her feet. “What did he do to warrant such evil behavior from you?!”

Empousa gawked at him. “Just a few? Mydei, tears were brimming in his eyes!”

“I thought you said he just looked like he was about to cry.”

Mydei rolled his eyes and took another sip of his coffee.

“Mydei,” Empousa whined and slumped back down into her seat. “What did he do to you? Do you really not want to tell me?”

He continued staring at the floor with images of their night at the club flashing through his mind once more. The argument over drink orders that really meant nothing in the long run, the blatant teasing and joking, and the kissing… He hadn't thought about Phainon in such a long time, even though his whole debut song centered around him.

“Nothing happened,” Mydei acquiesced to the stubborn woman. “I met him, gave him my number, and he ghosted me. That's it.”

“What happened to your energy two seconds ago?” With a light laugh, he patted Empousa’s back. “Weren't you just defending Phainon to the death and roasting me just now?”

“How could he ghost you?!” She slammed her hands on the cushioned seating underneath them, making Mydei jump in place. Well, her energy definitely returned. “He doesn't… He wouldn't do that!”

“You seem awfully confident for someone who just met him twenty minutes ago.”

“He wouldn't do that!” Jumping to her feet, she rushed out of the room, shutting the door behind her as quickly as she had come in. Silence suddenly enveloped the room he was in, with only the dull thrumming of the plane engines filling his ears once more. It was as if Empousa were never even here, and with a sigh, he relaxed back into the divan, plucking up his phone to entertain himself for the rest of the ride. That was, until the speakers turned on again. Did Herklas have something else he wanted to say? Maybe their time of arrival was being delayed for whatever reason?

“I already told you.”

Mydei's body froze at the sound of Phainon's voice. What was he trying to say over the speaker? And who was he talking to? This wasn't a typical pilot announcement; it sounded more like someone accidentally hit the button to broadcast his voice.

“You didn't tell me!” Empousa's voice rang clearly over the intercom.

“You can go ask Mydeimos. I don't think he wants to talk to me.” A sigh came after Phainon’s statement. “And I don't think I'm in a position to say.”

“You're going to tell Herklas and not me?” Empousa cried. “Mydei isn't telling me anything!”

Mydei scoffed to himself. She literally just ran out of his room after finding out the truth, so why did she run over to Phainon now?

“I only told him because I work in the cockpit with him.” Phainon laughed weakly. “I just thought… I don't know… It'd be awkward since we sit in the same room for hours on end.”

“So if I sat in the cockpit with you, would you tell me?”

“Empousa, there aren't enough seats for you, too, in the cockpit.”

“Okay, fine.” A slight pause before Empousa's voice returned. “Herklas, get up.”

Phainon laughed loudly–it was probably the happiest Mydei had heard Phainon since he locked eyes with him earlier. “Empousa, he's helping me drive the plane!”

“It's on autopilot right now! You think I don't know what altitude we're at? Herklas, get up!”

“Herklas, no!” Phainon cried.

“Herklas, get your butt out of the damn chair!”

Bickering could be heard between the new pilot and the flight attendant over the intercom, along with the sounds of a rough tussle, and Mydei had to hold in his laughter. What the Hell were they doing up there? And he was surprised Krateros was even allowing this to happen. Maybe he also felt bad for Phainon too, after suggesting to fire him, and wanted to leave the poor pilot alone for now.

“Fine, fine, fine! Leave Herklas alone!” Phainon's voice rang through the speaker once more. “I lost his number, okay?!”

A silence followed his words, and they slowly crept into Mydei's mind. It was so quiet that Mydei was unsure if they had found out the intercom was projecting their conversation the whole time, and they had finally shut it off.

What did he just say?

“You… what?” Empousa's voice echoed through the plane once more.

A loud, exasperated sigh came from Phainon. “He wrote his number down, and I fucking lost it, okay? And how the Hell am I, an average citizen, supposed to contact a fucking rockstar without his phone number? The cockpit door was slammed open, making two out of three people crowded into the cockpit jump in place.

“Mydei?!”

“Mydeimos?!”

Mydei was standing there, holding the cockpit door open, with the nastiest glare he had ever sent in someone’s way.

“You,” he growled toward Phainon, who was trembling like a leaf in his seat at the mere sight of him, “get over here.”

“H–Huh?” Phainon could barely manage an actual sound out of his mouth.

“Get–over–here.”

Phainon stood straight up as if possessed, rigidly dodging Empousa to stand right by Mydei’s side. What else was he supposed to do? Mydei was technically his boss.

Phainon was wondering the same damn thing! Why was the rockstar up here in the cockpit?!

“But.. why?” Empousa furrowed her eyebrows. “Why did you come up here?”

“Do you think I'm stupid?” Mydei glared at the flight attendant. “Or did you think I didn't hear every word?

Phainon just wanted to collapse.

“Wha–What?!” Both Phainon and Empousa screeched in the cockpit, and Herklas had to bring a hand up to his ear as he winced in pain.

“What do you mean you heard every word?!” Empousa cried. “Were you up here the whole time?! I just saw you in your room!”

“Your voices were being projected over the intercom.” Mydei furrowed his eyebrows. “You didn't realize?”

Empousa's eyes widened, and Phainon's jaw went slack. What was he talking about? Phainon wasn't holding the call button down. If both Empousa and Phainon were lost, there was only one other person with them in the cockpit who could've been holding the button down. Eyes widening in horror, he whipped his head toward Herklas, who was leisurely leaning his chin in the palm of his hand, watching the dramatic scene in front of him unfold.

“Herklas?!”

The co-pilot languidly shrugged. “Yes?”

Was Herklas just broadcasting their entire conversation the whole time?! Since when did he push the button, and for how long?! How much had Mydei heard of their conversation?! And why was Herklas even doing such a thing?! Sure, he met the guy about twenty minutes ago and probably spoke less than ten lines of dialogue with him that weren't shown in this story because the last chapter was in Mydei’s point of view, but he didn't seem like the type of guy to project their private conversation to everyone on the plane!

Whipping his head back toward the glowering rockstar, Phainon attempted every possible method to try to soothe the man. “My–Mydeimos, it's really not what you think–”

“My room. Now.”

Phainon shut his mouth immediately and followed Mydei out of the cockpit as if he had his tail between his legs, leaving Herklas to deal with the responsibility of driving the plane for now. Empousa, with her mouth agape, could only watch Phainon hesitantly trail after the fuming rockstar, with the door to his room shutting with a loud bang, rattling the various items that Mydei had set up in his room, such as his cup of coffee, phone, and other random miscellaneous items.

Mydei sighed tiredly, running a hand through his golden hair that Phainon so clearly remembered being so soft to the touch. He, unfortunately, remembered everything about this man–how he felt, how he tasted, how he acted, his facial expressions. Even though it had been so long ago, now that the rockstar was standing directly in front of him, it felt as if all his memories regarding this man returned to him all at once.

“Why are you calling me that?”

Phainon was jolted out of his thoughts upon hearing his beautifully smooth, deep voice. Yeah, Cipher's voice after thirty-three cocktails could never sound this good.

“Calling you what?”

“That name.” Mydei shapely pivoted on his feet, and Phainon almost hit the wall behind him to try and step out of his way. “I don't recall telling you that name.”

“Well… that's…” Phainon was too afraid to lock eyes with those glaringly golden ones. He just thought it was more professional, as a private pilot to his client, to call him by his given name. “Isn't that your name?”

“I didn't tell you that was my name,” Mydei retorted. “First of all, stop calling me that. It may be my full name, but I treat it as a stage name now. I don't like it when you call me that.”

“Yes, sir.”

“And look at me when you talk.”

“...Yes, sir.” Phainon slowly lifted his gaze from the floor, but Mydei's glare never ceased.

“Now, say it for me.”

“What?”

“My name.”

Phainon couldn't believe his face was heating up, even in this situation he was in. “...Mydei.”

Mydei laughed lightly; God, his smile looked so good on him. Phainon would do anything the man in front of him commanded him if he got to see that smile every time. “Good. Now tell me something.” Mydei crossed his arms, and Phainon was sad to see his smile disappear. “Did you even think about me at all?”

“Of course I did!” Phainon's eyes widened. Mydei just had no idea how often he thought about this rockstar standing in front of him. “I… I just really… didn't have any way to contact you.”

“Besides that number you lost.”

“Besides that number I lost.”

The rockstar ran another tired hand through his hair, exhaling deeply. “How the fuck did you lose my number? It better be a damn good reason.”

Grimacing, Phainon recalled the night that occurred many months ago. “To be completely honest, I don't know.”

He would've thought Mydei was going to throw a fit at that. How could he lose a celebrity’s number of all numbers? But the man continued to stay silent, so Phainon continued to explain.

“I left the club that night to carry my friend home, as you know. She's a really rowdy person, so she is extra… annoying when drunk. I was trying to carry her into the car, but she kept beating me up.”

Mydei coughed in an attempt to cover his laugh.

“Anyway,” Phainon continued, trying hard not to smile at the fact that Mydei found his unfortunate situation so amusing, “she kept punching and kicking me, but I finally managed to get her into the car. The next morning, I tried to text you to tell you everything, but I didn't have the napkin anymore.”

Mydei continued to stay silent at his explanation, but it seemed like he wanted to hear more of Phainon’s side of the story.

Obliging, Phainon attempted to recall the aftermath. “Because I couldn't really figure out how I could lose the napkin, I thought I was just so drunk I imagined you entirely. But when I–”

“You thought I was just an imagination?” Mydei raised an accusatory eyebrow.

“Well–That's–I–” Phainon just realized how bad that sounded. “You're… um… extremely… well… exactly…”

“Just spit it out.”

“You're exactly my dream man.” Phainon's face was bright red as he blurted out the first explanation he could think of. It was true, but he didn't want to word it so creepily to the object of his affection.

Mydei fell silent. Phainon didn't even want to look at the man anymore, and his eyes fell back to his black dress shoes. "So… um… I went to go ask my friend, Castorice, the one who found me with you, if she remembered you, and–”

He was wringing his fingers together and trying to focus on literally anything else except for the sheer embarrassment that was filling his entire being. Why did he have to word it like that? He could've said he was just so drunk he thought it was a dream, or that Mydei seemed too good to be true. But his dream man? Really?

The man in front of him scoffed. “So, you went to ask your friend if this dream man you met at the club the night before was real.”

He still couldn't believe that it even happened to him. What a stroke of bad luck.

“So my friend had the suggestion to look you up online, since I remembered your name,” Phainon continued the story. “He thought, maybe I could just message you online or something. Except… we… “

“Ended up finding out you were a celebrity.” Phainon's shoulders dropped, another sigh escaping him. “I… went back to the club. Every week, hoping that you would come back. One of the bartenders said you used to go there a lot, so I was just hoping you would be there. But, after a few months, I stopped–”

Phainon jumped, and he felt the back of his foot hitting the door behind him. Shit, was that weird? Was that crazy stalker level? Did he say months?

“Not–Not months.” Phainon swore he could feel nervous sweat running down his back. “It was… It was just like... A couple of weeks?”

“How many weeks?”

“Um…” Phainon furrowed his eyebrows. He bought an Old Fashioned almost every time he went, so he could probably just check his credit card statement to see how many times he bought a drink there. To be honest, though, he didn't want to see how much money he spent waiting for someone to mock him again for his drink order. “Maybe… eight? Nine? It wasn't more than fifteen weeks or so?”

Phainon fell silent.

“Maybe… Maybe…” Phainon was laughing like a maniac. He was just an extreme bundle of nerves at this point. “Maybe it was only like two weeks?” Phainon clearly remembered ordering way more than two Old Fashioneds.

Mydei narrowed his eyes. He definitely wasn't buying Phainon's obvious lie. “So was it two weeks or was it two months?”

“Anyway!” Phainon needed to move on from this conversation right now. “I never saw you again, and that was it. I was job hunting because I just graduated, and I got hired here. I found out you were working here when I looked up the company name after I got hired, but I didn't think we would… run into each other here. I'm sorry; if I knew, I would've asked to fly for someone else.”

“And why would you have asked for someone else?”

“Sorry?”

“If you knew the client was going to be me–” Mydei took a step forward, and Phainon tried to give him more space. But his back hit the wall, and he was suddenly pinned between the door and Mydei's piercing glare. “–you would have asked for someone else? Even after visiting the club, just to find me, for months?”

“Weeks!” Phainon squeaked. He was so dangerously close to the rockstar, and he wasn't sure if he could take much longer of this. If anything, he could twist the doorknob and bolt out of the room to escape back to the cockpit. Maybe Herklas will save him from the rockstar’s wrath; wait, no, he was in this situation in the first place because of his co-pilot. “It was just a few weeks!”

“Fine, whatever.” The golden-haired man rolled his eyes. “Let's just go with that stupid lie for now. You waited for me for… weeks, and now that you have an opportunity to see me again, you were just going to leave?”

The man in front of him clicked his tongue, but Phainon didn't know what expression he wore as he refused to look up at him. “You would voluntarily leave your dream man behind?”
