“I–Just answer her question, Mydei.” Phainon resorted to impatiently running his hand through his hair. He wasn't about to start with his misunderstanding of that song again. Other than when they made up and had quite the time in bed, he refused to recall any other memories from that night.

“What I think of Phainon?” Mydei stared at him with a frown, deep in thought. In fact, he was staring for so long that Phainon started anxiously fidgeting in his seat right next to the other man. What could he possibly be thinking about for so long?

“We can move on to another question if you want to think about it,” Aglaea suggested as she started scanning the room. “Should we do Cipher next?”

At the sound of her name, the woman sitting on the armrest perked up. “Oh! Oh! Let me get my phone!” She started digging all over the couch for her phone; most likely, she lost it in all the excitement during their earlier debate over the couple’s roles in bed.

But while she was scavenging the small couch and making everyone sitting on it stand up, Mydei opened his mouth. “It's hard to describe someone like Phainon.”

“Just go with your gut.” Aglaea smiled.

“My first thought is to call him an idiot.”

Phainon shoved Mydei in the shoulder.

“He is an idiot, but he is smart. He is stupidly insecure, but he is reliable.”

“Are you… complimenting me or making fun of me right now?”

Mydei continued without paying any attention to Phainon's words. “He is strong and dependable. He is always pestering me to do things with him, but I don't mind. Phainon is…” He took a deep breath. “Someone I would trust to have my back. Who wouldn't leave at the slightest hint of danger. That is who Phainon is to me.”

The room was silent, with even Cipher pausing in trying to find her phone. Phainon glanced around the room to gauge everyone’s reactions, but he was too busy trying to calm his own erratic heartbeat over Mydei's words that continued to echo in his head.

Someone I would trust to have my back

“That truly meant a lot to you, Phainon.” Another smirk from Aglaea, and Phainon immediately turned red.

“Well–That's–I… Of course it did,” Phainon mumbled with his shoulders slumping. He buried his face in the palms of his hands to hide his burning cheeks, which only earned laughter from around the room.

“Cipher, have you found your phone yet?”

“Yes, Aglaea!” Phainon heard Cipher exclaiming, and he chose to keep his head buried in his hands. Whatever question Cipher had for them could not be good.

“I tried to look up embarrassing shoe game questions, but I feel like most of the answers are obvious.” Phainon could hear Cipher tapping through her phone. “Like ‘Who is the better kisser?’ It's obviously not Phainon.”

“What do you mean it's obviously not me?!” Phainon's head shot up once more at the accusation, and he could faintly hear Mydei trying to cover his laughter with coughs once more.

Cipher hummed, ignoring Phainon's cries. “I kept scrolling and scrolling, but I don't think any of these are fun. ‘Who is messier?’ Definitely Phainon. ‘Who is better at cooking?’ Definitely Mydei.”

“You don't even know if Mydei can cook.”

“I definitely know that you can't cook, Phainon, unless it involves salad.”

Phainon stayed silent. He couldn't even deny it himself that Mydei was great at cooking.

“You know what!” Cipher suddenly exclaimed, making most of the room jump. “How did you guys make up? I want to hear both of your reactions to seeing each other at work. I'm sure that's an embarrassing story.”

“That's a good one!” Hyacine agreed, with Castorice pulling up her phone once more and nodding enthusiastically beside her. “You guys never told us how you guys made up.”

Mydei scoffed, leaning back against the wall as he recalled the story. “Phainon didn't know his voice was being projected over the intercom in the plane. He announced to the entire plane that he lost my number and didn't mean to ghost a celebrity.”

Over howls of laughter, Phainon scrambled to defend himself. “That wasn't me! The co-pilot was projecting my conversation with the flight attendant!”

“The look on your face when I came to the cockpit was priceless.” Mydei laughed to himself at the memory.

“How was I supposed to know my voice was being projected out there?!” Phainon was desperately clinging to Mydei's arm and shaking the man.

“So… So you found out Phainon lost your number… because of… Pfft.” Cipher's entire frame was shaking in a poor attempt to disguise her laughter.

“It wasn't my fault!”

“Well, Phainon, you have your co-pilot to thank for making up with your boyfriend.” Aglaea was trying to stifle her own laughter.

“Who's next?” It was Castorice’s turn to scan the room. “Did you want to go, Hyacine?”

“Yes! Yes, I do!” She cleared her throat as her own laughter came to a halt. “I want to know who said ‘I love you’ first. If you guys did,” Hyacine quickly added.

The two men stared at each other, with Phainon and Mydei furrowing their eyebrows at the same time. They definitely did, but who was first?

“Those exact words?” Mydei stared at the woman for clarification, who nodded fervently. “Then, I think it was you, Phainon.”

Phainon raised his eyebrows. “Really? I think it was you, Mydei.”

“It was definitely you.”

“Do you even have any proof?! Wasn't it you at the amusement park?”

“It was you in bed.”

“Wasn't that after though?!”

“That happened before the amusement park.”

“No, it didn't! What about the library?”

“I didn't say it in the library. Why would I tell you that in a library?”

The entire room watched as the two men continued bickering on the floor, trying to bring up different instances in which the other said the three words first. It eventually became a challenge of memory over who could think of the most experiences first, as the two men started referencing the different dates that they went on together throughout the past half a year, and keeping count of who thought of what first.

“Hyacine.” Anaxa heavily sighed as the two continued to argue and talk over the other person. “What have you done?”

“I–I didn't mean to spark such a debate.” Hyacine was staring with wide eyes at the two men who had started standing up from the floor to continue their heated argument. “I thought it was a straightforward answer.”

Another heavy sigh. “Do you think anything is straightforward with those two?”

“Anaxa, that's such a mean thing to say about someone you just met.” Hyacine giggled.

Anaxa immediately clicked his tongue. “Do not call me that.”

It was safe to say that Phainon and Mydei could not get through all eighteen questions before the night ended.
